newsitem.title: BURUNDI: U.N. envoy upbeat after talks in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy upbeat after talks in Burundi.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said on Monday he was optimistic about Burundi's future after talks with military leader Pierre Buyoya and opposition politicians.
"I think there is goodwill...I found no reservations concerning the need for a dialogue or the need for discussion," Sahnoun told a news conference at the end of a 24-hours visit.
"There were some clearly minor conditions which were expressed, (but) they are mainly dealing with confidence building measures rather than fundamental issues," said Sahnoun.

Sahnoun said he met Buyoya, leaders from the pro-Tutsi Uprona party and pro-Hutu Frodebu party, ousted president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya as well as diplomats and the leader of the National Assembly Leonce Ngendakumana.
Sahnoun, joint special representative of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) to the Great Lakes region, said:
"There is a will to bring together certain points of view and I must meet tomorrow (Tuesday) the facilitator in the region Mwalimu (teacher) Julius Nyerere."
Sahnoun was flying to Tanzania for the meeting.
Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels are fighting for a greater political stake in the ethnically divided tea and coffee growing country.
More than 150,000 people, mainly civilians caught in the middle, have died since 1993 when Tutsi soldiers murdered the first freely elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu.

Asked what Buyoya's attitude was towards serious negotiations with Hutu rebels, who mainly constitute Leonard Nyangoma's National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), Sahnoun said: "I think he is willing to participate in the talks. He is serious as far as I am concerned."
Marking the first anniversary last Friday of a bloodless coup that brought him to power, Buyoya promised to work for peace and unity.
All-party talks including CNDD are expected to take place next month in Arusha, north Tanzania. No exact date for the talks has been set.
